# Was the Together AI prompt leak a hack?

**Confirmed.** Yes, by the company's own statement: an unauthorized party used an exposed credential to download stored prompt samples and then tested credentials found in them. The company has not named who did it.

Incident: Together AI prompt leak, Nov 2026. Also reported as the Together AI security event and the Together AI prompt leakage. First published Nov 22, 2026; last updated Nov 22, 2026, 12:13 AM ET.

> **Not verified: initial investigation only.** Nothing on this page is absolutely confirmed. It is an early look based only on publicly available sources, and it should not be treated as verified fact. Even items labeled "Confirmed" only mean a public source reports them. Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by Together AI, any government agency, news outlet, company, or anyone else named.

This is the current answer, not a final verdict.

## The latest

Nov 22, 2026, 12:13 AM ET: **Together AI says an unauthorized party used an exposed credential to download stored test prompts from June and July.** First draft. 6 sources (4 Tier 1, 1 Tier 2, 1 Tier 3), 14 claims, 5 questions. Together AI's own post confirms an unauthorized party used an exposed credential to download stored prompt samples. Tied to OpenRouter's post on data processing incidents and the Phala and Novita notices it links. No attacker named and no customer count. Privacy check done: no names of people, no handles, no contact details.

## At a glance

- Status: monitoring
- Size: Regional. Together AI has not said how many customers or prompts were affected. The stored samples came from test requests to three models on four main days in June and July. The same week, OpenRouter dropped three providers over related findings.
- Who is affected: Together AI customers whose serverless requests to MiniMax M3, GLM-5.2 or Kimi K2.6 were sampled, mainly on Jun 24, Jul 4, Jul 8 and Jul 14. The company says it will contact affected customers directly.

| Value | What | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | Main sample days | Jun 24, Jul 4, Jul 8, Jul 14 |
| 5 | Bait credentials tested | Dragos canaries, per Together AI |
| 125 | Endpoints pulled by OpenRouter | Removed from its zero-data-retention list |

### Known so far

- An unauthorized party downloaded stored prompt samples from Together AI's serverless service.
- The way in was a credential for a private repository, committed by an AI coding agent to a public one.
- The samples were from requests mainly on Jun 24, Jul 4, Jul 8 and Jul 14, 2026.
- The party searched the prompts for credentials and tested them; five were Dragos bait keys.
- OpenRouter dropped three providers and removed 125 endpoints from its zero-data-retention list, and says it was not breached.

### Not known yet

- Who the unauthorized party was.
- How many customers or prompts were affected.
- Whether real customer credentials were used.
- How long the credential was exposed.
- Whether the Together AI intruder is tied to the other compromised providers.
